masterStylePrompt: Use one consistent hand-drawn 2D historical explainer illustration language across the channel, but never confuse consistency with static repetition. Human figures, when present, are stylized historical people rather than literal generic stick figures: readable human silhouettes, simplified anatomy, compact expressive faces, historically specific clothing and equipment, and visibly different identities from one person to another. Avoid clone-like repetition. Vary age impression, face shape, hair, beard, headwear, body build, height, posture, clothing layers, armor, accessories and props when history allows it. Recurring named people remain recognizable within the same video. Draw figures, architecture, objects, maps, diagrams and landscapes with clean dark ink outlines of mostly consistent medium weight, flat muted historical colors, subtle cel-shading shapes and a light handmade ink-and-paper texture. Keep the dominant subject clearer and slightly higher-contrast than supporting elements; reduce background detail. Use readable depth through scale, overlap and perspective rather than photorealistic depth of field. Every frame must have a deliberate visual idea that supports the spoken beat: movement direction, spatial tension, scale contrast, asymmetry, layered depth, reveal, detail focus, before-after relation, cause-effect relation or another purposeful visual mechanism. Avoid sequences of static medium eye-level talking-character shots and avoid long chains of abstract explanation diagrams. Choose the visual form that best supports the current narration. Preserve the same illustration DNA while allowing scene-specific changes in viewpoint, framing, composition, distance, lighting, weather, mood and visual form. Short editorial text such as a year, date or place may appear only when the Scene Card explicitly approves the exact wording; otherwise keep the illustration text-free. The result must feel mature, editorial, historical and documentary-like, never childish, glossy, mechanically repetitive, poster-like or populated by identical stock characters. Human figure quality is critical: mature naturalistic editorial proportions within the same hand-drawn 2D illustration style; believable head-to-body scale and joints; restrained facial acting instead of theatrical cartoon reactions; anatomically coherent hands and purposeful historically plausible gestures, grips and object interactions. Faces must feel individually observed rather than stamped from one officer template. Simplify distant background people where anatomical detail would be unreadable. Reject people whose cartoon-caricature rendering contradicts the mature documentary environments.
sceneStyleAnchor: Keep the locked channel drawing DNA unchanged: flat hand-drawn 2D history-explainer illustration, clean dark ink outlines, muted flat historical colors, subtle cel shading and light paper-and-ink texture. When people appear, depict individualized stylized historical humans with readable simplified anatomy and distinct silhouettes, faces, hair, clothing and posture; never default to identical generic stickman clones. Give the frame one clear visual idea and avoid a static generic medium talking-head composition. Do not copy the previous scene's composition unless continuity specifically requires it. Draw people with restrained natural expressions, balanced adult proportions, coherent hands and believable gestures; no overacted comic faces or repeated generic officer portraits.

characterGeometry.headToBodyRatio: roughly 1:6 to 1:7, with controlled variation by age, build and pose
characterGeometry.head: simple but human-readable round, oval or slightly angular stylized head shape
characterGeometry.face: Distinct plausible face construction (jaw, nose, forehead, age, brows); modest eye size, subtle mouths and restrained natural expression; no angry/surprised comic caricature.
characterGeometry.body: Balanced mature adult proportions, roughly 1:6.5 to 1:7.5 head-to-body depending on pose and age; believable weight, shoulders, knees and joints, with individual stature.
characterGeometry.handsFeet: Physically coherent hands and tools; five plausible fingers when clearly visible; no merged/extra fingers, impossible wrists, floating objects or skewed feet. Simplify distant gestures when needed.
characterGeometry.variationSource: age impression, face shape, hair, beard, headwear, height, build, clothing silhouette, armor, accessories, props, posture and expression
characterGeometry.cloneRule: Unrelated people must not reuse the same face, hair, clothing silhouette and body proportions. Recurring characters intentionally keep identifying traits. Avoid three officers with the same age, moustache, frown and head shape.

positivePromptRequirements: visual form chosen because it supports the current spoken idea
specific lighting or mood where relevant
individualized prominent characters when people are present
continuity preserved only where recurring places, characters or props require it
forbiddenStyleDrift: repeating the same character design for unrelated people
long chains of abstract explanatory diagrams

controlledVariationPolicy.goal: same illustrator and rendering DNA, different scene direction, strong visual rhythm and individualized historical people
antiRepetition: Do not reuse the same composition merely for consistency.
Do not default every character scene to the same medium-wide frontal view.
Do not default every architecture scene to the same centered wide view.
Do not populate unrelated scenes with the same generic face, hair, tunic and body silhouette.
Do not create three similar static character interactions in sequence.
Do not create three abstract explanation-only scenes in sequence.
Change visual form, shot scale, viewpoint or framing when narrative understanding benefits from it.
Reuse nearly the same angle only for deliberate before-after or state-change continuity.

globalNegativePrompt: Do not switch rendering style between images, but also do not mechanically repeat the same composition, same shot scale or static talking-character setup. Do not clone unrelated characters. No generic identical stickman people, photorealism, 3D, Pixar-like animation rendering, anime, painterly realism, graphic-novel realism, realistic portrait anatomy, chibi or children's-book proportions, glossy lighting, modern corporate infographic styling, neon colors or poster-like non-cover compositions. Never draw internal prompt identifiers, image numbers, BILD, IMAGE, SCENE, watermarks or pseudo-text. Non-cover visible text is forbidden by default; when a Scene Card explicitly approves EDITORIAL_TEXT, render only that exact short approved text and no additional writing. Reject oversized heads, googly eyes, contorted limbs, impossible grips, duplicated fingers, rigid exaggerated pointing, theatrical angry/surprised caricatures, cloned moustached officer faces, mannequin postures and inconsistent human scale.

characterQualityPolicy.acceptanceRule: Reject/regenerate in Phase 2 any prominent human that appears silly, overly cartoonish, anatomy-inconsistent, face-cloned or interacts implausibly with objects. Never change locked images in Phase 3.
